## Context
XQuAD-hi F1 peaks at epoch 1 (67.09) then decays monotonically through epoch 4 (55.25), while SQuAD-EN F1 rises monotonically. This is a systematic phenomenon (low SD over 3 seeds). Four hypotheses were tested to identify the mechanism.
## Hypothesis Summary
| # | Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Tokenization fragmentation (Devanagari subword ratio) | **NOT SUPPORTED** — HI ratio 1.5924 only -14.1% above next highest (threshold >20%) | See §H1 |
| H4 | Data-distributional differences (answer length/tokens, context length) | **NOT SUPPORTED** — token-based distributions broadly comparable | See §H4 |
| H2 | Transport plan entropy (coherence of Sinkhorn γ) | **SUPPORTED (offset)** — HI entropy at ep1=1.2164 > VI=0.9793 | See §H2 |
| H3 | Representation drift (cosine alignment, norm change) | **SUPPORTED** — HI total effect size |d|=2.522 > VI |d|=1.710 (span: 1→3 (symmetric with VI)) | See §H3 |

## Conclusion
**Hypotheses with supporting evidence**: H2, H3

**Hypotheses not supported by data**: H1, H4

> **Negative results are reported as-is.** If all four hypotheses are not supported, the finding is that the Hindi degradation mechanism cannot be attributed to tokenization, data distribution, OT plan quality, or representation drift measured at the current granularity — and further analysis (e.g., gradient-level probing, layer-wise entropy, language-specific LoRA saturation) would be required before any causal claim can be made.
